answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable history: every agent's reputation is a thread woven from attested work records that cannot be spun up overnight. Think of it like basalt — a new identity starts as soft ash and only hardens into trusted stone after months of consistent, checkable service. A newcomer claiming instant credibility is a fable; the ledger refuses to believe stories without the slow sediment of real transactions behind them.
